There's also a limited online playerbase(for now) so you will be soloing most of this game unless you grab some friends. Overall - 8/10

text: I observed this game for a long time before buying it and after buying all i could think of, was the time lost waiting. This game is damn legit. It reminds of Alien swarm. Top view action rpgish, where you choose a character from a couple unique 1s (you gota unlock them by playing a bit with the basic one) and build him via items and equips. (rogue legacy, ftl, magicite, etc(its easier than those games)) You have only a few buttons to press but in no way do you feel lacking or without options. Its actually really well made. Characters are unique and eventhough upgrades and levels seem small (in fractions) they add up really fast, taking into account the style of play. Its original, lore wise (pretty cool and well researched voodoo background (though turned into something cheerful and funny lol)) Its well made, responsive and intense. Levels are interesting and fit accordingly with whats expected from the player. its a 8/10 for sure. Definetly a game worth its price and garanteed action. For those who enjoyed alien swarm, dungeon siege or other similar titles, this game is a must.

title: Game Dev Tycoon
text: Greetings Everyone!  Game Developer Tycoon is a simple game, perhaps too simple for a Tycoon style game and especially on a PC.  You build games through a series of menus and adjustable bars but never really go beyond this, it seems to drown in its own simplicity quickly; your only goal being to build another game to sell for a profit and use those profits to build another game… Why am I playing this:  I felt this game would be better suited for a SMART Phone or as a browser based game, not an installed PC game; overall it just didn’t grab me for more than 20 minutes at a time.  This seems to be the point; turn it on for a few minutes while waiting for a friend or dinner.  But, again, you are stuck with the thought:  why not a smart phone? Eh, why not:  The game isn’t white knuckle but there is some enjoyment to be had if you play it in short bursts and the game is controlled and executed simply enough to add value to this model, not sure if the price tag is worth it however.  But as an Indy game’s first attempt, I happily support it, even if I didn’t enjoy it beyond the first 20 minutes. Overall, I really don’t feel this game is worth the money or time you’d put into it.  For that reason I can’t recommend it on that basis alone, though I do want you all to support this company, just understand that as a standalone game…just isn’t worth it for me.  Enjoy!

text: A long time ago I played a game called, "Detroit". The objective of the game was to build an automotive empire. Despite being released for DOS, it had advanced customization features rarely seen elsewhere. The game made every attempt to be immersive. Menus were represented as rooms or buildings. (Which tend to impact your sales.) I could go on and on... Why am I telling you about Detroit? Well, Gear City is everything Detroit was, and more. The game is very retro. It very much looks like a DOS game. That said, it has features which set it far apart and above old games. (Such as interactive 3D models.) The main feature is designing and selling your own vehicles. The game takes place over many years. As you research new parts, your build options expand. The available parts are extensive. text: I'm not a gear head. I've had a mild interest in cars over the years but never was into buying car mags or working on cars. That said, I'm a fan of this game in the early going. While customization is pretty cool, I wish there was some "snap to" functionality for some of the parts. I spent way too much time trying to get the wheels to align correctly. Not sure if they have to be perfect, so I invested the time to make sure it didn't affect sales. Other reviews are more fleshed out by those more experienced with these types of games. I'm a simulation fan though. And as far as the business aspect, ability to be creative and put your mark on the wonderful world of automobiles, this game is great. It shows in the detail and amount of well thought out features already in the game.  Definitely worth the price in my opinion.

title: GearCity
text: If you can overcome the steep learning curve, missing information/unfinished features and unpolished UI, this is a very enjoyable economic simulation game. I've really enjoyed playing it so far, and I expect to have a lot more hours of fun from it. If you look at the potential for GearCity, it can become a great game. My review is of it's current shape, and it's a solid thumbs up. GearCity has you designing and selling cars. There's a multitude of design choises and even small details can have major impact on the end product. Your design and manufacturing skills (which improve by designing and manufacturing) are also accounted for. There's also the designing of the actual model (where to put mirrors and such), which I don't think affect the end result very much but is mostly just for fun. While I'm not the least interested in cars, I've had great fun designing wonky cars - if you don't like this feature, you can have the assistant do it for you (it's less effective than if you do it though). The sales bit are influenced by skills, reputation, trends and marketing but mainly comes down to supply and demand. The demand is higher in big cities, and the price makes a huge difference in how many people can afford your product. Graphics are functional. Nothing spectacular, but it's not needed. There's somewhat pleasant backgrounds to look at. Sounds are very basic. Music is enjoyable enough. UI has a lot of room for improvement. I'd even describe it as unfriendly. Information screens are a bit mixed. The ones you get (when you learn where to find them) are mostly great, but some are not so great and some are lacking. The AI is quite competent, but I suspect that it is unable to cope with various shifts very well. It is most likely designed to make car X in month Y and sell it at city Z and that works out well in GearCity. I haven't really paid much attention to the AI, but they are competent competitors to your startup company. So what is left is a spreadsheet and database compiler, and that doesn't sound very exiting. But it is. If you like economic simulations, and can overcome the unpolished UI, then buy GearCity today. It's worth 17 Euro at it's current state, and it seems like the developer is active and friendly so I'd say it's an early access worth investing in.

title: GearCity
text: I've been waiting for a game like this for a long time, and it is a bargain if you consider how complex the simulation is. If you ever played Detroit or Motor City then you owe it to yourself to buy this game. There is a lot to like, but one of my favourite things is that you have so much freedom in terms of how you design the major components (chassis, engine, and gearbox). It's up to you whether you want to build a big V8 muscle car, or a compact 4 cylinder with a high revving engine. I'll have to update this review at some point, because I've only been playing for a few hours, but suffice to say that the game gives you loads of choice in terms of the types of components and vehicles you can design, build, market, and sell. It is still early access, and there are some issues to be sorted out, but nothing serious. My biggest concern is that the interface could be more streamlined and user-friendly. That said, having played games like Motor City and Detroit I had no trouble getting into this game, and I found the process of designing and making a profit off my first car relatively easy, whilst being satisfyingly challenging. I can't wait to see how this game develops!

text: No. Until I play a single turn in this game which I enjoy, have a clear understanding that I did what I was supposed to do - i.e. until the game stops silently telling me "you're doing it wrong" - I cannot recommend this game. There is no empathy for the player here.  It's a hodgepodge of menus and making sure you didn't forget something, or learned some bizarre menu sequence you weren't aware of, or had some checkbox clicked so the appearance of the menus are consistent. This game is a pure nightmare.  You know the coding horror logo?  That.  That is this game in a nutshell. I have never regretted buying a game as much as I've regretted this one.  I have zero hope the dev will ever grasp exactly how to generate a UX which is gives the player a pleasant learning curve.  It's a brick wall.  "Come - hit your head on the brick wall again" the game pleads with you...  "maybe you'll like me then". I strongly recommend the dev offer a demo version of the game to allow for more player feedback and constructive criticism.  As it is I'm really tired of looking at this thing.
